Text: Unlike their prokaryotic counterparts, eukaryotic RNA polymerases {{c1::cannot::can or cannot}} initiate transcription by themselves.
Back Extra:
Why: all five eukaryotic RNA polymerases need protein transcription factors, which must bind the promoter and build an initiation complex before the polymerase itself will bind and start the RNA chain.

Distinguish: the basal transcription factors are what initiation requires at all; enhancers and silencers, with still other factors, only tune how efficiently a promoter initiates.

must_test: eukaryotic RNA polymerases cannot initiate transcription by themselves (the contrast with prokaryotic polymerases, which can)

Text: In a promoter recognized by RNA polymerase II, the conserved element closest to the transcription start site (position +1) is the {{c1::TATA box}}, with consensus sequence {{c1::TATAAAA}} (read 5′ to 3′ on the nontemplate strand) and centered at about position {{c2::−30::position}}.
Back Extra:
Why: the TATA box plays an important role in positioning the transcription startpoint, and it is the element the first basal factor, TFIID, seats on through its TATA-binding protein.

Pitfall: the consensus is quoted from the nontemplate strand, the strand whose sequence matches the RNA; the template strand beneath it is the complement, ATATTTT.

The other transcription factors and RNA polymerase II join the complex in the sequence shown.' | Back Extra (unmarked, teaching only) p288 FIGURE 11.14 art, read on the render: the TATA box is drawn as 'ATATTTT' on the upper strand over 'TATAAAA' on the lower strand. | Stem frame only (unmarked context, no answer drawn from it) p287: 'The promoters recognized by RNA polymerase II consist of short conserved elements, or modules, located upstream from the transcription startpoint.'

Text: In an RNA polymerase II promoter, the {{c1::CAAT box}}, consensus sequence {{c1::GGCCAATCT}}, usually occurs near position {{c2::−80::position}}.
Back Extra:
Distinguish: the CAAT and TATA boxes sit at about the same positions in the promoters of most protein-coding nuclear genes, whereas the GC and octamer boxes may be present or absent and turn up at many different locations.

Cue: the box's name sits inside its consensus, GG-CCAAT-CT, so the real recall is the flanking letters.

consensus GGCCAATCT

Text: In RNA polymerase II promoters, the GC box has the consensus sequence {{c1::GGGCGG}}.
Back Extra:
Why: the GC box is an optional element, present in some RNA polymerase II promoters and absent from others, singly or in multiple copies at many different locations; when present it influences how efficiently the promoter initiates transcription.

Distinguish: the TATA and CAAT boxes, by contrast, sit at about the same positions in most protein-coding promoters.
verified_against: p288 (sentence carrying marks 48 and 49): 'Two other conserved elements, the GC box, consensus GGGCGG, and the octamer box, consensus ATTTGCAT, often are present in RNA polymerase II promoters; they influence the efficiency of a promoter in initiating transcription.' | Back Extra (unmarked, teaching only) p287 FIGURE 11.13 caption: 'The GC and octamer boxes may be present or absent; when present, they occur at many different locations, either singly or in multiple copies.' | Back Extra (unmarked, teaching only) p287 FIGURE 11.13 caption: 'The TATA and CAAT boxes are located at about the same positions in the promoters of most nuclear genes encoding proteins.'

must_test: GC box consensus GGGCGG
supporting: GC and octamer boxes are often present and influence promoter efficiency (unmarked remainder of the sentence, Why)
may be present or absent, many locations, singly or in multiple copies (caption, Why)
skip: no position is given on the page for the GC box, so none is carded (zero guessing)

Text: In RNA polymerase II promoters, the octamer box has the consensus sequence {{c1::ATTTGCAT}}.
Back Extra:
Why: like the GC box, the octamer box is an optional element that may be present or absent; when present it influences the efficiency of the promoter in initiating transcription.

Cue: an octamer is eight nucleotides, and the consensus is exactly eight letters long.
verified_against: p288 (sentence carrying marks 48 and 49): 'Two other conserved elements, the GC box, consensus GGGCGG, and the octamer box, consensus ATTTGCAT, often are present in RNA polymerase II promoters; they influence the efficiency of a promoter in initiating transcription.' | Back Extra (unmarked, teaching only) p287 FIGURE 11.13 caption: 'The GC and octamer boxes may be present or absent; when present, they occur at many different locations, either singly or in multiple copies.'

must_test: octamer box consensus ATTTGCAT

may be present or absent (caption, Why)

Text:
The first three basal transcription factors to interact with an RNA polymerase II promoter, in order of arrival, are:

1. {{c1::TFIID}} (the one carrying the TATA-binding protein)

2. {{c1::TFIIA}}

3. {{c1::TFIIB}}
Back Extra:
Meaning: each basal factor is written TFIIX, Transcription Factor X for RNA polymerase II, where X is a letter identifying the individual factor.

Why: the basal factors must interact with the promoter in the correct sequence for initiation to work, and RNA polymerase II itself does not bind until an initiation complex has formed.

Roster: TFIID → TFIIA → TFIIB → TFIIF (bringing RNA polymerase II) → TFIIE → TFIIH and TFIIJ.

Text: TFIID, the first basal transcription factor to interact with an RNA polymerase II promoter, contains a {{c1::TATA-binding protein}} ({{c2::TBP}}) plus several small proteins associated with it.
Back Extra:
Mechanism: the TATA-binding protein is what seats TFIID on the TATA box, the promoter element nearest the transcription startpoint; the other basal factors and RNA polymerase II then join around it.

Pitfall: TBP is one part of TFIID, not a separate basal factor; TFIID as a whole is what reaches the promoter first.

The other transcription factors and RNA polymerase II join the complex in the sequence shown.'
verified_by: drafter-D5; parenthetical-after-cloze warning cleared: '(TBP)' is the c2 blank of a two-way abbreviation pair, the sanctioned {{c1::term}} ({{c2::abbreviation}}) shape

Text: After TFIID, TFIIA and TFIIB are in place, the basal factor that joins next is {{c1::TFIIF}} — it first associates with {{c2::RNA polymerase II::enzyme}} so that the two enter the initiation complex together, and one of its two subunits has {{c3::DNA-unwinding}} activity.
Back Extra:
Why: with an unwinding subunit on board, TFIIF probably catalyzes the localized unwinding of the double helix that initiation requires; the polymerase needs a locally unwound segment, with one strand free to serve as template, before it can start.

Distinguish: TFIIH also unwinds DNA, but as the helicase that travels with RNA polymerase II during elongation; TFIIF's unwinding is for getting started.

Roster: TFIID → TFIIA → TFIIB → TFIIF (bringing RNA polymerase II) → TFIIE → TFIIH and TFIIJ.

Text: The basal factor that joins the initiation complex right after TFIIF and RNA polymerase II is {{c1::TFIIE}}, which binds the DNA {{c2::downstream::upstream or downstream}} from the transcription startpoint.
Back Extra:
Distinguish: TFIIE binding downstream of the startpoint is a fact about the RNA polymerase II complex; the thing that lies downstream in most RNA polymerase III genes is the promoter itself, inside the transcription unit.

Roster: TFIID → TFIIA → TFIIB → TFIIF (bringing RNA polymerase II) → TFIIE → TFIIH and TFIIJ.

must_test: TFIIE joins after TFIIF and RNA polymerase II
TFIIE binds the DNA downstream from the transcription startpoint

Text: Two more basal factors join the RNA polymerase II initiation complex after TFIIE — {{c1::TFIIH}} and {{c1::TFIIJ}} — but their locations in the complex are {{c2::unknown::known or unknown}}.
Back Extra:
Distinguish: of the pair, TFIIH is the one with a job beyond assembly; it is the helicase that travels with RNA polymerase II during elongation.

Roster: TFIID → TFIIA → TFIIB → TFIIF (bringing RNA polymerase II) → TFIIE → TFIIH and TFIIJ.

Text: {{c1::TFIIH}} has {{c2::helicase}} activity and travels with RNA polymerase II during {{c3::elongation::initiation or elongation}}, {{c2::unwinding}} the strands in the region of transcription (the transcription bubble).
Back Extra:
Distinguish: TFIIF also carries an unwinding subunit, but its unwinding is the localized opening of the helix needed to initiate; TFIIH is the helicase that stays with the polymerase and keeps unwinding through elongation.

Pitfall: TFIIH joins the initiation complex late, after TFIIE, and its seat there is unknown, yet it goes on working after initiation, riding with the polymerase.

Roster: TFIID → TFIIA → TFIIB → TFIIF (bringing RNA polymerase II) → TFIIE → TFIIH and TFIIJ.
